title: Differential alternative splicing in plant spaceflight transcriptomes: rMATS analysis of NASA OSDR RNA-seq data with machine learning and ontology integration
description: This deposit contains the results of a differential alternative splicing (AS) analysis of plant RNA-seq studies from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR). TODO: the analysis code is not yet included. Eight proof-of-concept studies were selected (7 Arabidopsis thaliana, 1 Brassica rapa; the OSD-59 Brassica outputs are not included), covering spaceflight, microgravity, Mars-level gravity, fractional gravity, simulated GCR radiation and lunar regolith. Across the 199 Arabidopsis samples (~100,000 splicing events), retained intron events were the largest class of significant events in 6 of 7 studies (51-72%). A frameshift heuristic that counts every retained intron as NMD-sensitive classified 79-86% of significant events as potentially NMD-sensitive. Cross-study recurrence identified 93 genes significant in >=2 studies, with AT4G17310 significant in 4 studies spanning gravity, radiation and regolith stressors. Differential splicing was quantified with rMATS-turbo v4.3.0 (FDR<0.05, |dPSI|>0.1). Machine learning (7-study LOSOCV classification, nested k-fold CV, UMAP clustering, SHAP feature importance) was applied to a 199-sample x 9,875-gene PSI feature matrix. Functional annotation used GO and MapMan bins. SpliceGrapher v0.2.7 was used for splice graph visualization.
